newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: PRESS DIGEST - Czech Republic - Feb 10.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Czech Republic - Feb 10.

text.p: PRAVO - After five days of talks, the railway strike, which was the largest single labour dispute since the establishment of the Czech Republic, ended on Saturday at one minute before midnight. The agreement made between the union and the cabinet requires, among other things, that Transport Minister Martin Riman present a proposal for transport strategy to the cabinet by the end of May.

- The five day railway strike caused many significant losses for many businesses dependent on railways. On Sunday, Vice-chairman of the cabinet, Josef Lux, estimated the losses at approximately one billion crowns.

HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - Farmers, who are unhappy with the state's intervention on the grains market decided to establish their own organisation which would trade this commodity and also regulate its price. At the end of last week, representatives from 34 district agrarian chambers signed a founding contract for the holding company Oblinarska Unie.

- On Friday, the crown once again reached a high against the German mark and passed the 16.7 limit. Information from domestic and foreign bank circles predicts that the crown could become one of the main European currencies in three years after the establishment of an EU currency.
- Reliable cabinet material states that the Czech National Bank estimates its net losses in amounts paid in deposits to insolvent banks, loans and grants at 32 billion crowns.

MLADA FRONTA DNES - The management of Budejovicky Budvar will obtain a majority share in the brewery only if it succeeds in increasing current production by one third by the end of the century. This is according to conditions for privatisation set out in a proposal from the Agriculture Ministry, which still must be approved by the cabinet.

- While the cabinet is carrying on unending debates about whether and how much patients should have to pay for health care, patients in some hospitals are already paying several thousands of crowns for better health care. This same possibility will soon be available for everyone.

LIDOVE NOVINY - The Sudeten Germans yesterday confirmed their disapproval of the Czech-German Declaration signed a few weeks ago by Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus and German Chancellor Helmut Kohl in Prague. A spokesman for the Sudeten Germans warned the city of Prague that before the Czech Republic will receive membership in the EU, there will be many opportunities to open the questions of Sudeten Germans' claims.
